heading: About the Rock Warblers

intro.lead: Welcome to the first event hosted by the Rock Warblers, our
intro.tail: at Adventure Off Road Park, Friday, June 19 through Sunday, June 21. Come join us for a weekend of fun, scaled adventure.

items.label: Rigs
items.text: 1/10 electric scale. 1.55″, 1.9″, and 2.2″ wheel classes. No dig, no rear steer. Five scale accessories minimum. No bashers.

items.label: The park
items.text: Adventure Off Road Park, South Pittsburg, TN — six hundred acres of private ridge. The pavilion is base camp: registration, driver meeting, hot dog dinner, awards, the 50/50 raffle, and the fire pit. Camping on-site, first come, first served.

items.label: The map
items.text: On-day reference built from GPS data and real terrain — the high-traffic hot spots and areas of interest around the park. Use it at the pavilion and out on each stage. Every line traces back to where it came from.

items.label: The crew
items.text: Rock Warblers — caw-craaawl! Kin to the Diamond-Billed Rock Pecker found only in Moab, Utah. Known for our bright blue shirts and ultimate scale builds. You'll find us mostly east of the Mississippi, with sightings in Canada, Pennsylvania, West Virginia, Michigan, and North Carolina. A rare breed has been spotted migrating between Europe and North America.

driver_meeting.heading: Driver's Meeting
paragraphs: Welcome, everyone, to the first event hosted by the Rock Warblers. You'll find us in the bright blue shirts, and we're so excited to have you here. The pavilion is home base for all the activities, and we meet there before each event. Several trails run off to the right of the pavilion, by the buggy entrance. Feel free to explore the Jeep entrance too, and document any fun trails on that side of the park. We'd love for everyone to run a GPS tracking app and share the areas you explored. We'll keep updating the map to show the hot spots and areas of interest around the park.
The C.O.W. is available throughout the day for your convenience. We've got batteries and basic necessities.
Trails are open to full-scale crawlers and bouncers this weekend, so keep your eyes and ears open and yield to the larger vehicles.

We're hosting a 50/50 raffle. Half goes to one lucky winner, and the other half goes to Appalachian RC for Kids. If you're not familiar with them, they're a West Virginia program that gives RC vehicles to kids under 12 who don't have one of their own. They're always at the BTC supporting the kids and helping fix RC cars that break down. Tickets are 5 for $10.

To kick things off, we'll set up the show and shine right out in front of the pavilion. After the show and shine, exploration begins. We've got a few challenges planned for today and tomorrow: the Warbler Peck and Pop Challenge, the Gravity Gauntlet, and PRO Line Before the Fire.

This evening, head back to the pavilion at 6pm for a hot dog dinner. Two hot dogs, chips, and a drink for $10. After dinner we'll run the PRO Line Before the Fire obstacle driving challenge, then head to the fire pit for s'mores.
On Sunday, we'll try our hand at GPS drawing during the Driver Doodles Sketchy Driving Challenge. At noon we wrap up with the awards ceremony, and then we clean, wrap, pack up, and head home.

items: Penalty points for gate touches, rollovers, and hogging.
Trail repairs and cleanup earn karma points that cancel penalties.
And most importantly, have some fun.

note: Made by the Rock Warblers. See you at the pavilion.
